How it works

HOW MUCH TO EAT ON THE BIKE

Carbohydrate is your main fuel at higher intensities. Your body only stores enough for a couple of hours of hard riding, so on longer or harder rides you need to top it up as you go, before you feel hungry or empty.

The rule of thumb

  • Under 1 hour: water is usually enough; for a hard session a small amount of carbs helps.
  • 1 to 2.5 hours: around 30–60 g per hour, more as the intensity goes up.
  • Over 2.5 hours: 60–90 g per hour, and up to 100–120 g for riders who have trained their gut.

Train your gut

Your gut can learn to absorb more carbs. Practise your race fuelling in training, starting lower and building up over a few weeks, and never try something new on race day. Products that mix glucose and fructose are absorbed better at high amounts.

Don't forget to drink

Most riders need around 500–750 ml of fluid per hour, more in the heat. Bottles with carbs and electrolytes help you cover both.
